newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates lower, few borrowers.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates lower, few borrowers.

text.p: * Central Bank not likely to change overnight rates
The Philippine interbank call loan rates dipped on Friday to an average of 11.03125 percent from 11.0625 as the market remained awash with money, traders said.
"The market was so liquid. There were not many borrowers. So market volume was pretty low," said a foreign bank dealer.
Done rates were from 11.03125 percent to 11.0625. Volume fell to 11.798 billion pesos from 16.679 billion.
Dealers said banks were still swamped with cash from the maturity of some 5 to 8 billion pesos of special series Treasury notes last Wednesday.
Due to the liquid market, one dealer said she doesn't expect the Central Bank to lower its overnight rates next week since this may give rise to peso speculation.
Last Monday, the Central Bank lowered its overnight rates by 1.50 percentage points after it raised its rates for two straight sessions the previous week to fight speculation.
In the secondary market, activity was muted because buyers opted to wait for the results of next Monday's weekly auction of Treasury bills, dealers said.
